It counts whitespace-separated words, case-insensitively (keys are lowercase).
Keys appear in the order each word is first seen.
reference:
use std.map
use std.str

pub fn word_count(text: Str) -> Map[Str, Int]
  var counts: Map[Str, Int] = {}
  for w in str.words(str.lower(text))
    set counts = map.update(counts, key: w, default: 0, f: fn(n) => n + 1)
  end for
  counts
end fn

    pub fn parse_pairs(text: Str) -> Result[Map[Str, Int], Str]

`text` holds `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, e.g. `"a=1;b=22"`. Surrounding
whitespace around keys and values is ignored; empty segments are skipped.
Return `Err("bad pair: <segment>")` for a segment without exactly one `=`, and
`Err("bad number: <value>")` when the value is not an integer.
reference:
use std.map
use std.str

pub fn parse_pairs(text: Str) -> Result[Map[Str, Int], Str]
  var out: Map[Str, Int] = {}
  for segment in str.split(text, ";")
    if str.trim(segment) == ""
      continue
    end if
    match str.split(segment, "=")
      case [key, value]
        match str.to_int(value)
          case Some(n) => set out = map.put(out, key: str.trim(key), value: n)
          case None => return Err("bad number: ${str.trim(value)}")
        end match
      case _ => return Err("bad pair: ${segment}")
    end match
  end for
  Ok(out)
end fn

  expect solution.parse_pairs(" x = -3 ;; ") == Ok({"x": -3})
  expect solution.parse_pairs("") == Ok({})
end test

test "invalid"
  expect solution.parse_pairs("a=1;b") == Err("bad pair: b")
  expect solution.parse_pairs("a=x") == Err("bad number: x")

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` defining a stack machine:

    pub type Instr
      case Push(value: Int)
      case Add
      case Mul
      case Dup
      case Pop
    end type

    pub fn run(program: List[Instr]) -> Result[List[Int], Str]

The stack starts empty and is returned top-last (the last pushed value is the
last element). `Add`/`Mul` pop two values and push the result; `Dup` pushes a
copy of the top; `Pop` removes the top. Any instruction that needs more values
than are on the stack returns `Err("stack underflow")`.
reference:
use std.list

pub type Instr
  case Push(value: Int)
  case Add
  case Mul
  case Dup
  case Pop
end type

pub fn run(program: List[Instr]) -> Result[List[Int], Str]
  var stack: List[Int] = []
  for instr in program
    set stack = step(stack, instr)?
  end for
  Ok(stack)
end fn

fn step(stack: List[Int], instr: Instr) -> Result[List[Int], Str]
  let n = list.len(stack)
  let rest2 = list.take(stack, n - 2)
  let top2 = list.drop(stack, n - 2)
  match instr
    case Push(v) => Ok(list.push(stack, v))
    case Add | Mul
      match top2
        case [a, b]
          if instr == Add
            Ok(list.push(rest2, a + b))
          else
            Ok(list.push(rest2, a * b))
          end if
        case _ => Err("stack underflow")
      end match
    case Dup
      match stack
        case [.._, top] => Ok(list.push(stack, top))
        case _ => Err("stack underflow")
      end match
    case Pop
      match stack
        case [..rest, _] => Ok(rest)
        case _ => Err("stack underflow")
      end match
  end match
end fn
tests:

test "arithmetic"
  expect solution.run([solution.Push(2), solution.Push(3), solution.Add, solution.Dup, solution.Mul]) == Ok([25])
  expect solution.run([]) == Ok([])
  expect solution.run([solution.Push(1), solution.Push(2), solution.Pop]) == Ok([1])
end test

test "underflow"
  expect solution.run([solution.Add]) == Err("stack underflow")
  expect solution.run([solution.Push(1), solution.Mul]) == Err("stack underflow")
  expect solution.run([solution.Dup]) == Err("stack underflow")
end test

Write `solution.veld` defining:

    pub fn to_roman(n: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]

Convert 1..3999 to Roman numerals (`4 -> "IV"`, `1994 -> "MCMXCIV"`).
Other inputs return `Err("out of range")`.
reference:
use std.list

record Numeral
  value: Int
  symbol: Str
end record

fn numerals() -> List[Numeral]
  [
    Numeral{value: 1000, symbol: "M"},
    Numeral{value: 900, symbol: "CM"},
    Numeral{value: 500, symbol: "D"},
    Numeral{value: 400, symbol: "CD"},
    Numeral{value: 100, symbol: "C"},
    Numeral{value: 90, symbol: "XC"},
    Numeral{value: 50, symbol: "L"},
    Numeral{value: 40, symbol: "XL"},
    Numeral{value: 10, symbol: "X"},
    Numeral{value: 9, symbol: "IX"},
    Numeral{value: 5, symbol: "V"},
    Numeral{value: 4, symbol: "IV"},
    Numeral{value: 1, symbol: "I"},
  ]
end fn

pub fn to_roman(n: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]
  if n < 1 or n > 3999
    return Err("out of range")
  end if
  var rest = n
  var out = ""
  for num in numerals()
    while rest >= num.value
      set out = out + num.symbol
      set rest = rest - num.value
    end while
  end for
  Ok(out)
end fn

  expect solution.to_roman(0) == Err("out of range")
end test

pub fn total(json_text: Str) -> Result[Float, Str]

    case Ok(JArr(items)) => items
    case Ok(_) => return Err("bad item")
    case Err(_) => return Err("invalid json")

  end for
  Ok(sum)

    pub fn search(xs: List[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]

`xs` is sorted ascending with no duplicates. Return the index of `target`
using binary search (O(log n) comparisons), or `None`.
reference:
use std.list

pub fn search(xs: List[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]
  var low = 0
  var high = list.len(xs) - 1
  while low <= high
    let mid = (low + high) / 2
    match list.get(xs, mid)
      case Some(v) if v == target => return Some(mid)
      case Some(v) if v < target => set low = mid + 1
      case _ => set high = mid - 1
    end match
  end while
  None
end fn

  expect solution.search(xs, 4) == None

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` defining:

    pub record Item
      sku: Str
      qty: Int
    end record

    pub type Event
      case Received(sku: Str, qty: Int)
      case Shipped(sku: Str, qty: Int)
    end type

    pub fn apply_events(stock: List[Item], events: List[Event]) -> Result[List[Item], Str]

Apply events in order. `Received` adds quantity (creating the item at the end
of the list if new). `Shipped` removes quantity; if the item is missing or
would go negative, return `Err("insufficient <sku>")`. Items keep their order.
reference:
use std.list

pub record Item
  sku: Str
  qty: Int
end record

pub type Event
  case Received(sku: Str, qty: Int)
  case Shipped(sku: Str, qty: Int)
end type

pub fn apply_events(stock: List[Item], events: List[Event]) -> Result[List[Item], Str]
  var items = stock
  for e in events
    set items = match e
      case Received(sku, qty) => adjust(items, sku: sku, delta: qty)
      case Shipped(sku, qty)
        let current = list.find(items, fn(i) => i.sku == sku)
        match current
          case Some(i) if i.qty >= qty => adjust(items, sku: sku, delta: -qty)
          case _ => return Err("insufficient ${sku}")
        end match
    end match
  end for
  Ok(items)
end fn

fn adjust(items: List[Item], sku: Str, delta: Int) -> List[Item]
  if list.any(items, fn(i) => i.sku == sku)
    list.map(items, fn(i) => adjust_one(i, sku: sku, delta: delta))
  else
    list.push(items, Item{sku: sku, qty: delta})
  end if
end fn

fn adjust_one(i: Item, sku: Str, delta: Int) -> Item
  if i.sku == sku
    Item{..i, qty: i.qty + delta}
  else
    i
  end if
end fn

test "events"
  let stock = [solution.Item{sku: "a", qty: 2}]
  let events = [solution.Received(sku: "b", qty: 5), solution.Shipped(sku: "a", qty: 2)]
  expect solution.apply_events(stock, events) == Ok([solution.Item{sku: "a", qty: 0}, solution.Item{sku: "b", qty: 5}])
  expect solution.apply_events(stock, [solution.Shipped(sku: "a", qty: 3)]) == Err("insufficient a")
  expect solution.apply_events([], [solution.Shipped(sku: "z", qty: 1)]) == Err("insufficient z")

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` implementing a turnstile:

    pub type State
      case Locked
      case Unlocked(coins: Int)
      case Broken
    end type

    pub type Event
      case Coin
      case Push
      case Kick
    end type

    pub fn step(state: State, event: Event) -> State
    pub fn run(events: List[Event]) -> State

Rules for `step`:

- `Coin` unlocks a locked turnstile with 1 coin; on an unlocked one it adds a coin.
- `Push` locks an unlocked turnstile again; on a locked one nothing happens.
- `Kick` breaks it, whatever state it is in. A broken turnstile ignores everything.

`run` starts from `Locked` and applies the events in order.
reference:
use std.list

pub type State
  case Locked
  case Unlocked(coins: Int)
  case Broken
end type

pub type Event
  case Coin
  case Push
  case Kick
end type

pub fn step(state: State, event: Event) -> State
  match state, event
    case Broken, _ => Broken
    case _, Kick => Broken
    case Locked, Coin => Unlocked(1)
    case Locked, Push => Locked
    case Unlocked(n), Coin => Unlocked(n + 1)
    case Unlocked(_), Push => Locked
  end match
end fn

pub fn run(events: List[Event]) -> State
  list.fold(events, init: Locked, step: step)
end fn

test "single steps"

  expect solution.step(solution.Unlocked(2), solution.Coin) == solution.Unlocked(3)
  expect solution.step(solution.Unlocked(2), solution.Push) == solution.Locked
  expect solution.step(solution.Locked, solution.Push) == solution.Locked
  expect solution.step(solution.Unlocked(1), solution.Kick) == solution.Broken
  expect solution.step(solution.Broken, solution.Coin) == solution.Broken
end test

test "runs"

  expect solution.run([solution.Coin, solution.Kick, solution.Coin, solution.Push]) == solution.Broken
end test

use std.list
use std.str

pub fn route(method: Str, path: Str) -> Str
  let segments = str.split(path, "/") |> list.filter(fn(s) => s != "")
  match method, segments
    case "GET", [] => "home"
    case "GET", ["users"] => "list users"
    case "POST", ["users"] => "create user"
    case "GET", ["users", id] => "show user ${id}"
    case "DELETE", ["users", id] => "delete user ${id}"
    case _, [] => "405"
    case _, ["users"] => "405"
    case _, ["users", _] => "405"
    case _ => "404"
  end match
end fn

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` with

    pub fn totals(text: Str) -> Result[List[Str], Str]

`text` is CSV with a header line `category,amount` followed by data rows, for
example `food,12`. Sum the amounts per category and return one line per
category, formatted `category: total`, sorted by category name.

- Fields may be quoted (`"office, misc",5`).
- A row that does not have exactly two fields, or whose amount is not an
  integer, makes the whole result `Err("bad row N")`, where N is the line
  number of the row counting the header as line 1.
- A missing or different header is `Err("bad header")`.
- Blank lines are ignored (and do not count as rows).
reference:
use std.csv
use std.list
use std.map
use std.str

pub fn totals(text: Str) -> Result[List[Str], Str]
  let rows = csv.parse(text)?
  match rows
    case [] => Err("bad header")
    case [header, ..data]
      if header != ["category", "amount"]
        return Err("bad header")
      end if
      var sums: Map[Str, Int] = {}
      var line = 1
      for row in data
        set line = line + 1
        match row
          case [category, amount]
            match str.to_int(amount)
              case Some(n) => set sums = map.update(sums, key: category, default: 0, f: fn(total) => total + n)
              case None => return Err("bad row ${line}")
            end match
          case _ => return Err("bad row ${line}")
        end match
      end for
      let names = list.sort(map.keys(sums))
      Ok(list.map(names, fn(name) => "${name}: ${map.get_or(sums, key: name, default: 0)}"))
  end match
end fn

Write `solution.veld` with

    pub fn emails(text: Str) -> List[Str]
    pub fn is_iso_date(text: Str) -> Bool
    pub fn redact_digits(text: Str) -> Str

- `emails` returns every email address in the text, in order. An address is
  letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, then `@`, then a domain of labels made of
  letters, digits and `-`, separated by dots, ending in a dot and at least two
  letters (`bob.smith@mail.example.com`).
- `is_iso_date` is true for exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` with a month 01-12 and a day
  01-31 (it does not need to know month lengths).
- `redact_digits` replaces every run of digits with a single `#`.
reference:
use std.regex

pub fn emails(text: Str) -> List[Str]
  match regex.find_all("""[A-Za-z0-9._-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,}""", text)
    case Ok(found) => found
    case Err(_) => []
  end match
end fn

pub fn is_iso_date(text: Str) -> Bool
  match regex.is_match("""^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$""", text)
    case Ok(ok) => ok
    case Err(_) => false
  end match
end fn

pub fn redact_digits(text: Str) -> Str
  match regex.replace(text, pattern: """\d+""", with: "#")
    case Ok(out) => out
    case Err(_) => text
  end match
end fn

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` implementing a least-recently-used cache of Int values:

    pub record Cache
      capacity: Int
      order: List[Str]          # keys, least recently used first
      values: Map[Str, Int]
    end record

    pub fn new(capacity: Int) -> Cache
    pub fn put(cache: Cache, key: Str, value: Int) -> Cache
    pub fn get(cache: Cache, key: Str) -> Pair[Option[Int], Cache]

`put` inserts or updates a key and makes it the most recently used one. When
that would exceed `capacity`, the least recently used key is evicted first.
`get` returns the value (`None` if absent) together with the cache in which that
key has become the most recently used. A capacity below 1 behaves like 1.
`Pair` is a prelude record with fields `first` and `second`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.map
use std.math

pub record Cache
  capacity: Int
  order: List[Str]
  values: Map[Str, Int]
end record

pub fn new(capacity: Int) -> Cache
  Cache{capacity: math.max(capacity, 1), order: [], values: {}}
end fn

fn touch(order: List[Str], key: Str) -> List[Str]
  list.push(list.filter(order, fn(k) => k != key), key)
end fn

pub fn put(cache: Cache, key: Str, value: Int) -> Cache
  var order = cache.order
  var values = cache.values
  if not map.has(values, key) and list.len(order) >= cache.capacity
    match list.first(order)
      case Some(oldest)
        set order = list.drop(order, 1)
        set values = map.remove(values, oldest)
      case None => set order = order
    end match
  end if
  Cache{..cache, order: touch(order, key), values: map.put(values, key: key, value: value)}
end fn

pub fn get(cache: Cache, key: Str) -> Pair[Option[Int], Cache]
  match map.get(cache.values, key)
    case Some(v) => Pair{first: Some(v), second: Cache{..cache, order: touch(cache.order, key)}}
    case None => Pair{first: None, second: cache}
  end match
end fn

use std.json
use std.list
use std.map
use std.math

record Person
  name: Str
  age: Int
end record

fn person(j: Json) -> Option[Person]
  let name = json.get(j, "name")?
  let age = json.get(j, "age")?
  match name, age
    case JStr(n), JNum(a) => Some(Person{name: n, age: math.round(a)})
    case _ => None
  end match
end fn

pub fn summarize(text: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
  let doc = match json.parse(text)
    case Ok(d) => d
    case Err(e) => return Err(e)
  end match
  let items = match doc
    case JArr(items) => items
    case _ => return Err("expected an array")
  end match
  var people: List[Person] = []
  var index = 0
  for item in items
    match person(item)
      case Some(p) => set people = list.push(people, p)
      case None => return Err("bad person at index ${index}")
    end match
    set index = index + 1
  end for
  let count = list.len(people)
  let total = list.sum(list.map(people, fn(p) => p.age))
  let oldest = match list.max_by(people, key: fn(p) => p.age)
    case Some(p) => json.string(p.name)
    case None => JNull
  end match
  let average = if count == 0
    0.0
  else
    math.to_float(total) / math.to_float(count)
  end if
  let names = list.sort(list.map(people, fn(p) => p.name))
  Ok(
    json.encode(
      json.object(
        {
          "count": json.int(count),
          "oldest": oldest,
          "average_age": json.number(average),
          "names": json.array(list.map(names, json.string)),
        },
      ),
    ),
  )
end fn

Matrices are lists of rows. `transpose` swaps rows and columns (`[]` stays `[]`;
all rows have equal length). `multiply` is the matrix product of an m x n and an
n x p matrix; if the inner dimensions differ it returns `Err("dimension mismatch")`.
`identity(n)` is the n x n identity matrix (`[]` for n <= 0).
reference:
use std.list

pub fn identity(n: Int) -> List[List[Int]]
  list.map(
    list.range(0, n),
    fn(i)
      list.map(
        list.range(0, n),
        fn(j)
          if i == j
            1
          else
            0
          end if
        end fn,
      )
    end fn,
  )
end fn

fn width(m: List[List[Int]]) -> Int
  match m
    case [] => 0
    case [row, .._] => list.len(row)
  end match
end fn

fn cell(m: List[List[Int]], row: Int, col: Int) -> Int
  match list.get(m, row)
    case Some(r) => list.get(r, col) |> unwrap_int()
    case None => 0
  end match
end fn

fn unwrap_int(o: Option[Int]) -> Int
  match o
    case Some(v) => v
    case None => 0
  end match
end fn

pub fn transpose(m: List[List[Int]]) -> List[List[Int]]
  list.map(list.range(0, width(m)), fn(c) => list.map(m, fn(row) => unwrap_int(list.get(row, c))))
end fn

pub fn multiply(a: List[List[Int]], b: List[List[Int]]) -> Result[List[List[Int]], Str]
  if width(a) != list.len(b)
    return Err("dimension mismatch")
  end if
  let bt = transpose(b)
  Ok(list.map(a, fn(row) => list.map(bt, fn(col) => dot(row, col))))
end fn

fn dot(xs: List[Int], ys: List[Int]) -> Int
  list.sum(
    list.map(list.range(0, list.len(xs)), fn(i) => unwrap_int(list.get(xs, i)) * unwrap_int(list.get(ys, i))),
  )
end fn

    pub fn wrap(text: Str, width: Int) -> List[Str]

Greedy word wrap: split `text` into words (runs of non-space characters) and pack
as many words as fit on each line, separated by single spaces, so that no line is
longer than `width` characters. A word longer than `width` gets a line of its own
(it is not split). Text without words gives `[]`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.str

pub fn wrap(text: Str, width: Int) -> List[Str]
  var lines: List[Str] = []
  var current = ""
  for word in str.words(text)
    if current == ""
      set current = word
    else if str.len(current) + 1 + str.len(word) <= width
      set current = current + " " + word
    else
      set lines = list.push(lines, current)
      set current = word
    end if
  end for
  if current != ""
    set lines = list.push(lines, current)
  end if
  lines
end fn

    pub fn shortest(edges: List[Edge], from: Str, to: Str) -> Option[Int]

`edges` describe a directed graph with non-negative costs. Return the cost of the
cheapest path from `from` to `to`, `Some(0)` when they are the same node, and
`None` when `to` is unreachable (or a node does not appear at all). The graph can
have thousands of edges: the solution must be much faster than trying every path.

Call it with named arguments, as Veld requires for three or more parameters:
`shortest(edges, from: "a", to: "b")`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.map

pub record Edge
  from: Str
  to: Str
  cost: Int
end record

fn adjacency(edges: List[Edge]) -> Map[Str, List[Edge]]
  var out: Map[Str, List[Edge]] = {}
  for e in edges
    set out = map.update(out, key: e.from, default: [], f: fn(es) => list.push(es, e))
  end for
  out
end fn

pub fn shortest(edges: List[Edge], from: Str, to: Str) -> Option[Int]
  let graph = adjacency(edges)
  var dist: Map[Str, Int] = {from: 0}
  var done: Map[Str, Bool] = {}
  while true
    var best: Option[Str] = None
    var best_cost = 0
    for node in map.keys(dist)
      if not map.has(done, node)
        let d = map.get_or(dist, key: node, default: 0)
        match best
          case None
            set best = Some(node)
            set best_cost = d
          case Some(_)
            if d < best_cost
              set best = Some(node)
              set best_cost = d
            end if
        end match
      end if
    end for
    match best
      case None => break
      case Some(node)
        set done = map.put(done, key: node, value: true)
        for e in map.get_or(graph, key: node, default: [])
          let candidate = best_cost + e.cost
          match map.get(dist, e.to)
            case Some(existing)
              if candidate < existing
                set dist = map.put(dist, key: e.to, value: candidate)
              end if
            case None => set dist = map.put(dist, key: e.to, value: candidate)
          end match
        end for
    end match
  end while
  map.get(dist, to)
end fn
